title: EnvironmentDefinition
description: How to create, start, deploy into, observe and reset one environment instance. The adapter implements the lifecycle (PLAN.md §5); this file only parameterises it.

adapter.description: A registered adapter kind (PLAN.md §5, §9). `local-web` is the MVP world; `local-db` is a file-backed one. Either way the adapter is an implementation of the lifecycle, not an environment: Veridian ships worlds, and a world may be simulated.

app.description: Directory of the application under test, relative to this file.

env.description: Environment variables. Values are treated as untrusted.

dependencyInstall.description: Command run once before start, inside `app`. Null means the app has no dependencies to install.

command.description: Executed verbatim, not through a shell string built from user input.

readyPattern.description: A regular expression matched against stdout to decide the app has started. Use this instead of sleeping.

url.description: Base URL of the running app, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4317. Null or absent for a world reached by opening a file rather than over a socket - a database world has no address, and spelling that as an empty string would make 'this world has no address' indistinguishable from 'nobody filled the field in'.

databasePath.description: Path of the database file this world is, relative to this file (or absolute). Present for a file-backed world such as `local-db`, where the application's state IS this file; absent for every other world. Stated here rather than as an adapter-private option so the plan every reader sees names the same file the adapter opens.

path.description: Appended to `url` to form the probe address. Null when there is no url to append to.

expectStatus.description: The status a healthy probe returns, defaulted only for a world reached over HTTP. Null hands the verdict to the adapter's own readiness signal, which is the only honest shape for a world that has no status to return.

reset.description: Reset is first-class (PLAN.md §20). A validator must never inherit contaminated state from a previous run.
